questions.q: What table does the Problem table (`problem`) extend in ServiceNow?
options: The base `task` table, the same table Incident extends
The Incident table directly
The Change Request table
It does not extend any other table
questions.explain: Both `problem` and `incident` extend `task`, which is why a Problem record's base fields look structurally familiar.

questions.q: What is the real field-level mechanism that links an Incident to a Problem?
options: A `problem_id` reference field on the Incident table pointing at the Problem record
Copying the Incident's short description into the Problem record
A shared `sys_id` between the two records
There is no field-level link; it's tracked only in a spreadsheet
questions.explain: The Incident table carries a `problem_id` reference field; populating it points that Incident at the matching Problem record.

questions.q: On a Problem record, how does an agent see every Incident linked to it?
options: A related list on the Problem record automatically shows every Incident whose `problem_id` points back at it
By manually re-typing each Incident number into a text field on the Problem
Linked Incidents are not visible from the Problem record at all
Only an admin can view linked Incidents, via a background script
questions.explain: The related list is live and auto-populated from the `problem_id` reference — no manual maintenance needed.

questions.q: What is the single biggest implementation risk this lesson identifies for Problem Management?
options: Agents failing to find an existing Problem record and opening a redundant duplicate investigation instead of linking to it
The Problem table lacking a priority field
Incidents being impossible to close while a Problem is open
The Problem table having too many required fields
questions.explain: Redundant Problem records split root-cause effort and documentation across multiple records instead of consolidating it in one.

questions.q: How does an Incident's scope differ from a Problem's scope, per this lesson?
options: An Incident represents one instance of disruption; a Problem represents the underlying cause that may be generating many Incidents
They represent exactly the same scope with no meaningful difference
A Problem is always smaller in scope than any single Incident
Incidents are closed automatically whenever a Problem is created
questions.explain: This is the core distinction the table design reflects: one instance of disruption versus the shared root cause behind potentially many instances.
